hypothesis: The bench datadir lives on tmpfs (/tmp on AL2023); a real node uses XFS on EBS. Moving it to $HOME (XFS, noatime, gp3) checks whether file-system reads matter here. The DB is rebuilt from genesis every run, so pages should stay hot in the page cache: expect no change.
llm_commentary: Datadir on XFS (EBS gp3, noatime) instead of tmpfs is neutral on c8a (4.68s), c8g (6.74s) and m9g (4.58s). c8i's 5.68s (+3.3% vs the 5.50s control) coincides with a step change that also hit the closing control (5.73s), so it is host drift, not XFS. As expected for this benchmark: the database is created from genesis at node start and stays in the page cache, so read-side file-system tuning (readahead, mount options) has nothing to act on. It would matter for a node whose state exceeds RAM, which this workload does not model.
